title: The Man Who Was Never Headed: Alex Baker's Long Walk to Catalonia
title_candidates: The Man Who Was Never Headed: Alex Baker's Long Walk to Catalonia
Three Spoons and a Trophy: Baker Leads From the Fifth Hole to the Last
From Wooden Spoon to Silverware: Alex Baker's Catalan Coronation
Forty-Six, Then Hold On: How Alex Baker Won TEG 18
The 106 and the 169: Alex Baker Contained Multitudes at Camiral
theme: The most decorated Spoon-collector in the field led from the fifth hole of the first round and never gave it back — not because he played beautifully, but because he wrapped two field-best rounds around some of the ugliest golf in Camiral's records, and nobody else could keep pace with even that.
tone: house — subverted gravitas, British English, restraint and exact detail with occasional farcical escalation; tongue-in-cheek but never zany
opening_hook: Open on the fifth green of Round 1 at the Tour course, where Alex Baker — three prior Wooden Spoons, two of them in the last three TEGs — took a lead he would hold for 67 further holes; then act two shows what that lead had to survive (a 106, an 11, a 10), and act three shows nobody taking it off him.
foreshadow: Baker arrives with three Wooden Spoons and two in the last three TEGs — the least likely name on the trophy
He takes the outright lead at the 5th on the opening day and, though nobody knows it yet, that is the last lead change of the tournament
Jon Baker arrives as defending Trophy champion and holds the Jacket lead into R2 — both will be gone by the 2nd hole of R3
The Stadium course has never surrendered a round under 89 in 27 prior TEG visits

headline_candidates: Forty-Six at the Tour: Baker Takes a Lead and Keeps It
Patterson Bleeds Twenty-Two Shots in Eight Holes and Still Isn't Last
rounds.chosen_headline: Forty-Six at the Tour: Baker Takes a Lead and Keeps It
rounds.angle: Alex Baker's 46 points — best in the field by 12 — is the round that decides the tournament, built on a 17-point burst from the 8th to the 12th; behind him the field disintegrates in every direction, Patterson bleeding 22 shots from the 3rd to the 10th, Williams making a 9 and an 8, Mullin an 11 at the 15th, Jon Baker sliding to the bottom of the Spoon race at the last.

headline_candidates: One Hundred and Six: Baker Sets a Record He Cannot Have Wanted
An Eleven at the Last, and Still Eleven Clear
Jon Baker's Jacket Slips at the Seventh
rounds.chosen_headline: One Hundred and Six: Baker Sets a Record He Cannot Have Wanted
rounds.angle: The leader posts the worst gross round in the Tour course's 22-visit TEG history — 106, with a quintuple at the 16th and an 11 at the 18th — and emerges still 11 points clear, which tells you rather a lot about everyone else; meanwhile Williams answers a poor R1 with 42 points and takes the Jacket lead off Jon Baker at the 7th after 20 holes in front.

headline_candidates: Eighty-Four: Mullin Breaks the Stadium Record and Loses the Jacket By Fourteen
Williams Takes the Jacket at the Second and Jon Baker Takes the Spoon at the Same Hole
Twenty-One Points in Six Holes: Baker Restores Order
rounds.chosen_headline: Eighty-Four: Mullin Breaks the Stadium Record and Loses the Jacket By Fourteen
rounds.angle: The decisive day on all three fronts — Mullin's 84 is a new Stadium course record and a personal best there, yet at the 2nd hole Williams takes the Jacket lead for good and Jon Baker drops to the bottom of the Spoon race for good; Alex Baker answers with 44 points and 21 in six holes from the 11th to restore a 12-point cushion.

headline_candidates: A Ten, an Eight, and a Trophy
Williams Signs for 84 and the Jacket; Baker Signs for a Coronation
The Champion Makes Ten at the Fourteenth and Wins By Eight
rounds.chosen_headline: A Ten, an Eight, and a Trophy
rounds.angle: Baker's closing 38 is his worst round and includes a sextuple-bogey 10 at the 14th and an 8 at the 17th, and it does not matter a jot; Williams closes with a field-best 12 gross points and a personal best 84 at the Stadium to take the Jacket by 14, Mullin bleeds nine shots from the 14th, and Jon Baker finishes last for the third time in four rounds.

players.arc: Three prior Wooden Spoons and two in the last three TEGs, he seized the lead at the 5th hole of R1 and held it for the rest of the tournament, wrapping two field-best rounds (46, 44) around the worst gross round in the Tour course's TEG history and a sextuple-bogey 10 at the Stadium's 14th — the least tidy dominant victory imaginable, and a second Trophy.

Runner-up who out-scored the champion in two of the four rounds and never came close to the lead, bleeding 22 shots between the 3rd and 10th in R1 before recovering with new personal bests at both Camiral courses.

Reigning Wooden Spoon holder who went from bottom of the Spoon race at the 2nd in R2 to the Green Jacket by 14, taking the gross lead at the 2nd in R3 and never losing it, closing with a personal-best 84 at the Stadium.

Defending Trophy champion and Jacket leader for the first 20 holes he held it, who then made a quintuple-bogey 9 at the 4th in R3, dropped to the bottom of the Spoon race at the 2nd hole of that round, and finished 23 points adrift of the next worst man — dethroned by his own brother.

Nine-time Jacket winner who broke the Stadium course record with an 84 in R3 — his personal best there by seven — and still lost the Jacket by 14, bookending it with an 11 at the 15th in R1 and nine dropped shots from the 14th in R4.

venue_notes: TEG's 4th visit to Catalonia and, by now, deeply familiar ground: R1–R2 on the Tour course (5th and 6th TEG rounds there), R3–R4 on the Stadium (6th and 7th). Frame the Tour as the 'slightly more forgiving' sibling that nonetheless yielded a new course-worst 106, and the Stadium as Spain's premier championship test that surrendered its lowest ever TEG round (84) on the same day it inflicted a quintuple-bogey 9 and, next day, a 10. The gap between the resort's brochure and the scorecards is the running joke; keep it dry.

trophy_storyline.subject: Alex Baker's wire-to-wire Trophy win from the least likely CV in the field
trophy_storyline.why_it_matters: A man with three Wooden Spoons and two in the last three TEGs led from the 5th hole of the opening round to the end and won by 8, despite posting the worst gross round in the Tour course's TEG history in between.
trophy_storyline.shape: Setup: he takes the outright lead at the 5th in R1 on the way to 46 points, best in the field by 12, built on a 17-point run from the 8th to the 12th (b40). Turn: the lead then has to survive its owner — a 106 gross at the Tour in R2, a new course-worst (cr02), with a quintuple at the 16th and an 11 at the 18th (b36), then a sextuple-bogey 10 at the Stadium's 14th in R4 (b25). Resolution: he answered every wobble immediately — 44 points in R3 including 21 in six holes from the 11th (b04) — and closed with his worst round, 38, still eight clear of Patterson (b01), the steadiest man in a field that could not punish him.

jacket_storyline.subject: Gregg Williams builds the Green Jacket out of a ruined opening round
jacket_storyline.why_it_matters: The reigning Wooden Spoon holder made a 9 and an 8 on the first day, then won the gross by 14 — and won it on a specific hole on a specific day.
jacket_storyline.shape: Setup: R1 on the Tour is a shambles — a quadruple-bogey 9 at the 7th (b24), an 8 at the 17th (b20), the bleeding stopped only by a birdie at the 15th (b31) — and he sits third. Turn: he follows the poor R1 with a strong R2 (b42), taking the Jacket lead off Jon Baker at the 7th after 20 holes in front (b48), then makes it outright and permanent with a par at the Stadium's 2nd in R3 (b28) after four holes without a dropped shot (b21). Resolution: a field-best closing 12 gross points and a personal-best 84 at the Stadium give him the Jacket by 14 (b02), his third.

spoon_storyline.subject: Jon Baker, defending champion, takes the Wooden Spoon by 23
spoon_storyline.why_it_matters: The man who won TEG 17 and led the Jacket for the first 20 holes he held it finished last in three of four rounds and 23 points adrift of the next worst — the most comprehensive Spoon in the field's recent memory.
spoon_storyline.shape: Setup: he leads the Jacket from the 5th in R1 yet still slips to the bottom of the Spoon race at the 18th that same day (b84 territory aside, b48 records the lead he held). Turn: R2 briefly redeems him — 16 points from the 14th to the 18th without dropping a gross shot (b09, b13) — before R3 undoes everything: a quintuple-bogey 9 at the 4th (b39) and the drop to the bottom of the Spoon race at the 2nd, from which he never returned. Resolution: 28 and 29 points to close, last in the field again, 126 in total and 23 behind Mullin (b14).

discovered_storylines.subject: The Stadium course record broken and immediately rendered pointless — David Mullin's 84
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: The lowest gross round ever recorded on the Stadium in TEG history, achieved by the nine-time Jacket winner, and it still lost him the Jacket by 14.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: Mullin's tournament opens with an 11 at the Tour's 15th (b35) that sends him to the bottom of the Spoon race on the spot (b66). Turn: in R3 he posts 84 gross at the Stadium — a new course record, beating 89 across 27 prior visits (cr01) — and a personal best there by seven. Resolution: it buys him nothing; he bleeds nine shots from the 14th to the 17th in R4 (b45, b49) and finishes second in the Jacket by 14 (b02).

discovered_storylines.subject: The brothers Baker at opposite ends of the same tournament
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Alex Baker won the Trophy from a CV of three Wooden Spoons; his brother Jon, the defending champion, took the Spoon by 23 — the whole spread of TEG 18 sits inside one family.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: after R1 and R2 the leaderboards read Alex Baker top of the Trophy, Jon Baker top of the Jacket (b81-era reporting, recorded in b37). Turn: Jon loses the Jacket lead at the 7th in R2 (b48), makes a quintuple-bogey 9 at the Stadium's 4th in R3 (b39) and drops to the bottom of the Spoon race; Alex answers with 44 points and 21 in six holes (b04). Resolution: Alex takes the Trophy by 8 (b01) while Jon collects the Spoon on 126 (b14) — 43 points between brothers.

discovered_storylines.subject: Camiral's catalogue of catastrophe: the double-figure holes and the record-worst round
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Across four rounds on two courses the field produced two 11s, a 10, a 9, a 9, several 8s and the worst gross round the Tour course has ever seen in TEG — and the champion owned a share of them.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: R1 sets the tone — Patterson bleeds 22 shots from the 3rd to the 10th (b18) with a quadruple-bogey 8 at the 3rd, Williams makes 9 at the 7th (b24), Mullin an 11 at the 15th (b35). Turn: R2 escalates it to the record books, Alex Baker signing for 106, a new Tour course-worst (cr02), with an 8 at the 16th (b46) and an 11 at the 18th (b36). Resolution: the Stadium takes over — Jon Baker's 9 at the 4th in R3 (b39) and Alex Baker's sextuple-bogey 10 at the 14th in R4 (b25) — and the trophy still went to the man with most of them.

payoffs.payoff: The same man signs for 169 points and a second Trophy, the field's most decorated Spoon-collector now its champion.

payoffs.payoff: Confirm the leaderboard: leader after every round, gap never below 8, three lead changes all inside the first five holes of R1 and none thereafter.

payoffs.seed: Jon Baker arrives as defending champion and Jacket leader
payoffs.payoff: He loses the Jacket lead at the 7th in R2 after 20 holes in front (b48) and drops to the bottom of the Spoon race at the 2nd in R3, never to return — finishing 23 adrift (b14).

payoffs.seed: The Stadium has never surrendered a TEG round under 89 in 27 prior visits
payoffs.payoff: Mullin posts 84 (cr01) — and loses the Jacket by 14 anyway; Williams matches the number in R4 for his own personal best and takes the Jacket.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Taken up as a supporting vehicle — the double-figure holes and the record-worst 106 are genuinely a catalogue — but it rides behind `underdog`, because the story of TEG 18 is that the man with three Wooden Spoons and most of the catastrophes won the thing.

why_the_champion_won: Two best-in-field rounds (46 in R1, 44 in R3) either side of a Tour-course-worst 106, and the steadiest week in the field — never worse than 3rd of 5 in any round — while John Patterson out-scored him in two rounds and was never close enough for it to matter: the margin was as much inherited as built, and Baker was simply the man in position to take it.
